decks.title: Building agents with Google ADK 2.0
decks.description: Google ADK 2.0 from the first agent to production: graph workflows, plugins, YAML, skills, managed agents, verifiers, evals, AgentOps and the newest agent design patterns (October 2026).
decks.brief:
Google ADK 2.0 (current 2.13.0, Oct 2026) and the newest agent design patterns. The user demands, explicitly:
- Latest material only (Oct 2026). NO outdated "ReAct 1.0" style content — classic ReAct only as one line of history.
- Google platform: Agentspace -> Gemini Enterprise, managed agents (Vertex AI Agent Engine / ManagedAgent), Antigravity, Agent Starter Pack, Agents CLI.
- ADK 2.0: Workflow graph API (edges, routing, fan-out/fan-in, loops, dynamic @node/ctx.run_node, collaborative modes chat/task/single_turn, RequestInput HITL, RetryConfig, checkpoint/resume), App, plugins, YAML Agent Config + declarative YAML graphs, Agent Skills / SkillToolset, tools/MCP/A2A, sessions/state/memory/artifacts, context caching + compaction, multimodal handling (images/audio/video/files, artifacts, Live API bidi streaming).
- Engineering disciplines: context engineering, loop engineering, graph engineering, harness engineering, per-step verifiers, evals (adk eval, rubrics, user simulation, trajectory), guardrails/security, best practices checklist, AgentOps (observability, OTel GenAI, CI eval gates, deployment, cost).
- Agentic design patterns implemented in ADK 2.0 with the latest patterns (orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer, generator-verifier, router, parallel fan-out, deep agents, subagents for context isolation, HITL, memory).
- Frequent useful code snippets (about every second slide), real codelabs quoted with URLs.
decks.ctx: a university-grade 60-slide deck teaching Google Agent Development Kit (ADK) 2.0 (latest as of Oct 2026) and agentic design patterns, from first principles to production.

topics: 01-adk2-whats-new

ADK 2.0 vs ADK 1.x: release announcement(s), release notes, CHANGELOG at github.com/google/adk-python, breaking changes, migration guide, new primitives (graph-based workflows, App class, resumability, HITL, plugins, context caching, event compaction, etc.). Exact PyPI google-adk versions + dates. ADK Java/Go/TypeScript status. adk CLI (create, web, run, api_server, deploy, eval) and Dev UI.
02-workflows

Workflow orchestration in ADK 2.0: SequentialAgent, ParallelAgent, LoopAgent, custom BaseAgent (_run_async_impl), the 2.0 graph workflow model (nodes, edges, conditional routing, fan-out/fan-in), state passing (output_key, {state} templating), escalate/exit_loop, checkpoints/resume, HITL, long-running tools. Exact code + execution semantics (events, invocation, branch).
03-codelabs

ALL Google codelabs on ADK (search codelabs.developers.google.com for ADK, Agent Development Kit, Agent Engine, A2A, MCP Toolbox). For each: exact title, URL, what is built, key steps, key code. Prioritise 2025-2026 and ADK 2.0. 15+ codelabs. Also Kaggle 5-Day AI Agents Intensive (Nov 2025) and Google Cloud Skills Boost ADK materials.
04-core-concepts

ADK core concepts with exact current APIs: LlmAgent/Agent params (name, model, instruction, description, tools, sub_agents, output_key, output_schema, generate_content_config, planner, code_executor), Runner/InMemoryRunner, App, SessionService types, State prefixes (user:, app:, temp:), MemoryService + Vertex AI Memory Bank, Artifacts, Events, contexts (InvocationContext, ToolContext, CallbackContext), callbacks, plugins, delegation (transfer_to_agent, AgentTool), bidi streaming (Live API), models (Gemini 2.5/3, LiteLLM).
05-tools-mcp-a2a

ADK tools: FunctionTool, built-ins (google_search, code execution, Vertex AI Search, BigQuery), OpenAPI toolset, MCPToolset (stdio / streamable HTTP), exposing ADK as MCP server, MCP Toolbox for Databases, LongRunningFunctionTool, tool confirmation, tool auth, A2A protocol (RemoteA2aAgent, to_a2a, agent card), deployment to Vertex AI Agent Engine, Cloud Run, GKE, Agent Starter Pack. Code + commands.
06-eval-observability-safety

ADK evaluation and safety: adk eval, evalsets, metrics (tool_trajectory_avg_score, response_match_score, final_response_match_v2, LLM-as-judge, hallucination, safety), user simulation, tracing (OpenTelemetry, Cloud Trace, Phoenix etc.), guardrails via callbacks/plugins, Model Armor, prompt-injection defence. Key ideas of Google whitepapers "Agents", "Agents Companion", Kaggle 2025 agent whitepapers.
07-design-patterns

Agentic design patterns: Antonio Gulli "Agentic Design Patterns" (2025, 21 patterns, list all), Anthropic "Building effective agents", Google Cloud Architecture Center agentic design pattern guide, Andrew Ng 4 patterns, ReAct, plan-and-execute, generator-critic, hierarchical decomposition, HITL, memory, agentic RAG, guardrails, resource-aware routing. For EACH: definition, when to use, failure modes, ADK implementation sketch (code).
08-video-community

YouTube/community on ADK 2025-2026 (Google Cloud Tech, Google for Developers, I/O 2025/2026, Cloud Next 2025/2026, Agent Factory podcast, Kaggle livestreams): title, channel, URL, date, takeaways. google/adk-samples agents (customer-service, data-science, financial-advisor, travel-concierge, llm-auditor, academic-research, etc.): architecture + patterns. Adoption stats (stars, downloads).
01-context-engineering

Context engineering as the core discipline of agent design (2025-2026): definitions (Anthropic "Effective context engineering for AI agents", LangChain, Manus "Context Engineering for AI Agents: Lessons from Building Manus", Google ADK context/compaction features), write/select/compress/isolate, KV-cache-aware design, context rot, compaction, note-taking/scratchpads, just-in-time retrieval, tool result offloading to filesystem, Agentic Context Engineering (ACE) paper, 12-factor agents.
02-harness-deep-agents

Modern agent harness architectures: "deep agents" (planning tool + virtual filesystem + subagents + detailed system prompt; LangChain deepagents), Claude Agent SDK / Claude Code architecture, OpenAI Agents SDK + Codex, Google ADK 2.0 graph workflows, long-horizon agents, durable execution (Temporal, Restate, DBOS, Vercel Workflow, LangGraph durable), agent loops vs workflows (Anthropic "Building effective agents" updated view), Agent Skills (Anthropic skills, progressive disclosure), code execution with MCP ("code mode", Cloudflare + Anthropic posts), tool design for agents (Anthropic "Writing effective tools for agents").
03-multi-agent-2026

Multi-agent systems as of 2026: Anthropic "How we built our multi-agent research system" (orchestrator-worker, token usage numbers), Cognition "Don't build multi-agents" debate and the reconciliation, subagents for context isolation, A2A protocol v0.3+/Linux Foundation, agent cards, AP2 (Agent Payments Protocol), MCP latest spec (2025-06-18 / 2025-11 versions: elicitation, structured output, OAuth, tasks), handoffs vs agents-as-tools, swarm vs hierarchical, Google ADK multi-agent primitives in 2.0.
04-computer-browser-coding-agents

Frontier agent types 2025-2026: computer-use agents (Gemini 2.5 Computer Use, OpenAI Operator/ChatGPT agent, Claude computer use), browser agents, coding agents (Jules, Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI) and their patterns (plan mode, sandboxes, test-driven loops, checkpoints), deep research agents, voice/live agents (Gemini Live API, ADK bidi streaming), background/async agents, scheduled agents. Benchmarks: SWE-bench Verified, OSWorld, tau2-bench, Terminal-Bench, GAIA, BrowseComp, METR time-horizon trend (numbers as of 2026).
05-reliability-eval-safety

Agent reliability, eval and safety 2026: eval-driven agent development, trajectory evals, LLM judges with rubrics, simulation-based evals (tau-bench style user simulators), ADK eval + user simulation, observability (OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions), guardrails, prompt-injection defences (CaMeL, dual-LLM, Google "defense in depth" for Gemini agents, Meta "Agents Rule of Two"), human-in-the-loop approvals, least-privilege tools, agent identity/auth, cost/latency control (model routing, caching).
06-learning-memory-agents

Agents that improve: long-term memory architectures (Vertex AI Memory Bank, Mem0, Letta, Zep), memory as files, self-improving agents (reflection memory, ACE playbooks, Agent Workflow Memory), agentic RL (RL fine-tuning of agents on tool use: e.g. Kimi K2/K2-Thinking, DeepSeek V3.1/V3.2 agent training, OpenAI RFT, Search-R1, verl agent training), reasoning models + tools interleaved thinking, model-native agent capabilities in Gemini 3 / Claude 4.5 / GPT-5 era.
01-agentspace-gemini-enterprise

Google Agentspace and its evolution into Gemini Enterprise (dates, editions, pricing tiers if public), Agent Gallery, Agent Designer (no-code), connectors, registering ADK agents into Gemini Enterprise / Agentspace (steps, commands), A2A agents in Gemini Enterprise, Google-built agents (Deep Research, NotebookLM Enterprise, Idea Generation, Data Science agent), governance. Agent Marketplace / Google Cloud Marketplace for agents.
02-managed-agents-agent-engine

Managed agents on Google Cloud as of Oct 2026: Vertex AI Agent Engine (now possibly "Agent Engine" in Vertex AI / Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform — verify naming), deploy ADK with adk deploy agent_engine and the Python SDK (vertexai.agent_engines / AdkApp), Agent Engine Sessions, Memory Bank, Code Execution sandbox, Example Store, observability, pricing model, Agent Starter Pack, Cloud Run and GKE deployment alternatives, Agent Identity / IAM for agents. Codelabs + code.
03-antigravity

Google Antigravity (agentic development platform/IDE, launched with Gemini 3, Nov 2025): Agent Manager / mission control, editor view, browser agent, artifacts (task lists, implementation plans, walkthroughs, screenshots, recordings), review/feedback loop, models supported, knowledge base, how teams use it to build ADK agents; plus Gemini CLI, Jules, Firebase Studio relationship. Latest updates through Oct 2026. Codelabs/tutorials.
04-adk2-workflows-graph

ADK 2.0 workflows in full detail: graph-based workflow API (nodes, edges, routers, conditional edges, joins, loops, subgraphs), how it differs from SequentialAgent/ParallelAgent/LoopAgent, state schema/typed state, checkpointing/resume, human-in-the-loop interrupts, long-running operations, streaming of intermediate events, visualising graphs in adk web. Exact code from source/docs/samples. Also ADK release notes 2.x through Oct 2026.
05-adk2-yaml-plugins

ADK Agent Config (YAML agent definitions: root_agent.yaml, keys like agent_class, model, instruction, sub_agents, tools, config_path; adk create --type=config), its 2.0 status, and ADK Plugins (BasePlugin, plugin callbacks before_run/after_run/on_event/before_model/after_model/before_tool/after_tool/on_model_error/on_tool_error, registering plugins on Runner/App, built-in plugins e.g. LoggingPlugin, ReflectAndRetryToolPlugin, context filter, global instruction plugin, BigQuery analytics plugin), callbacks vs plugins. Real YAML and Python code.
06-loop-graph-engineering

The newest engineering disciplines for agents (2025-2026): "loop engineering" (designing the agent loop: stop conditions, budgets, max iterations, reflection/critique loops, retry with feedback, escalation), "graph engineering" (explicit control-flow graphs vs autonomous loops, when to hard-code edges, hybrid graphs with LLM routers), "context engineering", "harness engineering", "flow engineering" (AlphaCodium), evaluator-optimizer, verifier-in-the-loop. Find who coined/uses each term and the best articles/talks. Map each to ADK 2.0 implementation.
07-verifiers-evals

Per-step verifiers and evals for agents: step-level verification (programmatic checks, schema validation, unit tests, LLM-judge with rubric, process reward models), verifier placement in graphs, guard nodes, ReflectAndRetry patterns, self-consistency/majority vote, eval-driven development, ADK evaluation (adk eval, evalsets, tool trajectory metrics, rubric-based metrics, user simulation, hallucination/safety metrics in latest ADK), Vertex AI Gen AI evaluation service for agents, online vs offline evals, regression gates in CI. Code.
08-best-practices-2026

Agent engineering best practices as of Oct 2026, consolidated from: Google (ADK docs best practices, Google Cloud "agent" architecture guides, Gemini 3 prompting/agent guides, Startup technical guide: AI agents), Anthropic (Building effective agents, Writing effective tools, Effective context engineering, Claude Agent SDK best practices, long-running agent harness posts), OpenAI (A practical guide to building agents, Agents SDK docs, GPT-5 prompting guide), LangChain State of Agent Engineering reports, 12-factor agents. Cover: start simple, tool design, instructions/system prompts, structured outputs, state design, memory, error handling, cost/latency budgets, model selection/routing, security (least privilege, prompt injection), HITL, observability, evals-first, deployment, versioning. Make a checklist.
09-multimodal-adk

Multimodal handling in ADK 2.0 and Gemini (Oct 2026): sending images/audio/video/PDF to agents (types.Part, inline_data vs file_data / Files API), Artifacts (save_artifact/load_artifact, ArtifactService, GCS), multimodal tool results, image generation/editing tools (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image "Nano Banana", Imagen, Veo) inside agents, bidi streaming voice/video with Live API in ADK (run_live, LiveRequestQueue, RunConfig, StreamingMode, native audio models, session resumption), media resolution and token costs per modality, Gemini 3 multimodal capabilities, document understanding. Exact code from docs/samples + codelabs (e.g. ADK streaming codelabs).
10-multimodal-patterns

Multimodal agent design patterns 2025-2026: multimodal RAG for agents, vision-grounded computer use (Gemini 2.5 Computer Use model via ADK ComputerUseToolset), screenshot-action loops, voice agents architecture (cascaded STT-LLM-TTS vs native audio), latency budgets, interruption/barge-in handling, video understanding pipelines, image-generation workflows with critique loops, multimodal evals. Real products/case studies.
11-agentops-lifecycle

AgentOps as of Oct 2026: definition and lifecycle (build -> evaluate -> deploy -> observe -> improve), Google Cloud view (Agent Starter Pack CI/CD with Cloud Build, Terraform, eval gates; Vertex AI Agent Engine observability; Cloud Trace/Logging; BigQuery agent analytics plugin; "AgentOps" in Google whitepapers e.g. Kaggle "Prototype to Production" / Agents Companion), versioning of prompts/agents/tools, canary + shadow deployments, A/B for agents, rollback, CI eval regression gates, cost/latency/token SLOs, incident response for agents, feedback loops from production traces into eval sets, prompt/agent optimization (ADK adk optimize GEPA).
12-agentops-tooling

AgentOps tooling landscape Oct 2026: OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions (status, span names like invoke_agent / execute_tool / chat), ADK telemetry (AutoTracingPlugin, otel_to_cloud), Langfuse, Arize Phoenix/AX, LangSmith, Braintrust, Weights & Biases Weave, Datadog LLM Observability, Galileo, AgentOps.ai, Helicone, MLflow 3 GenAI tracing; agent registries and governance (Gemini Enterprise agent registry, A2A agent cards, MCP registries), identity for agents (agent identity in IAM, workload identity), guardrails at runtime (Model Armor), cost management and model routing. Comparison table + code for wiring ADK to OTel/Cloud Trace and one third-party tool.

decks.title: Retrieval-augmented generation, October 2026
decks.description: RAG from first principles to the state of the art: ingestion, chunking, embeddings, hybrid search, reranking, agentic RAG, GraphRAG, multimodal RAG, evaluation, security and production.
decks.brief: RAG from first principles to the state of the art as of Oct 2026: why RAG, ingestion/parsing, chunking, embeddings, vector indexes, hybrid search + RRF, reranking, query transformation, contextual retrieval, long-context vs RAG, agentic RAG (router, Self-RAG, CRAG, Adaptive-RAG, multi-hop, deep research agents, RL-trained search agents, MCP retrieval), GraphRAG/LightRAG/HippoRAG/RAPTOR, DRAG/DRAGIN, multimodal RAG (ColPali), memory, evaluation (RAGAS etc.), security (indirect prompt injection, poisoning, ACLs), production/cost/latency, managed RAG (Vertex AI RAG Engine, Gemini File Search, etc.). All patterns. Real practical examples, codelabs and GitHub repos quoted with URLs. Code snippets about every third slide.
decks.ctx: a university-grade 60-slide deck teaching Retrieval-Augmented Generation from first principles to the state of the art as of Oct 2026, including agentic RAG and every major pattern, with real practical examples.

topics: 01-foundations

RAG foundations: why RAG, Lewis et al. 2020, ingestion/parsing (Docling, Unstructured, LlamaParse, Gemini doc parsing), chunking (fixed, recursive, semantic, late chunking, contextual headers, parent-child), embeddings (top MTEB 2026: Gemini embedding, OpenAI text-embedding-3, Voyage, Cohere embed v4, Qwen3-Embedding; Matryoshka), vector indexes (HNSW, IVF, PQ, DiskANN, ScaNN), metrics. Numbers.
02-advanced-retrieval

Hybrid search (BM25+dense, RRF), SPLADE, ColBERTv2, ColPali/ColQwen, rerankers (cross-encoders, Cohere Rerank, Voyage, Jina, BGE, LLM rerankers), query transforms (multi-query, RAG-Fusion, HyDE, step-back, decomposition), metadata filtering, self-query, Anthropic Contextual Retrieval (their numbers), long-context vs RAG 2025-2026, context caching, lost-in-the-middle.
03-agentic-rag

Agentic RAG: survey arXiv 2501.09136 taxonomy, router RAG, ReAct retrieval agents, Self-RAG, CRAG, Adaptive-RAG, IRCoT, FLARE, plan-and-execute, multi-agent RAG, Deep Research agents (OpenAI, Gemini, open_deep_research, GPT Researcher), RL-trained search agents (Search-R1, R1-Searcher, ReSearch, DeepResearcher), MCP as retrieval interface. LangGraph and Google ADK code.
04-graph-structured

GraphRAG (Microsoft: entity extraction, Leiden, global/local/DRIFT, LazyGraphRAG), LightRAG, HippoRAG 2, RAPTOR, KG-RAG with Neo4j, text-to-SQL RAG, hybrid KG+vector. Research all real meanings of "DRAG" in RAG literature (cite papers) and DRAGIN. Benchmarks + costs.
05-multimodal-memory

Multimodal RAG (images, tables, charts, video; ColPali; multimodal embeddings), code RAG, conversational RAG + memory (Mem0, Letta, Zep/Graphiti, Vertex AI Memory Bank), cache-augmented generation, personalization, real-time/streaming RAG, on-device RAG.
06-eval-ops-security

RAG eval and ops: RAGAS metrics, TruLens RAG triad, ARES, LLM-as-judge, benchmarks (BEIR, MTEB, KILT, HotpotQA, FRAMES, BrowseComp, MultiHop-RAG), observability (Langfuse, Phoenix, LangSmith), latency/cost, caching, guardrails, security (indirect prompt injection, PoisonedRAG, ACL-aware retrieval, PII), freshness + incremental indexing.
07-platforms-codelabs

ALL Google codelabs on RAG (Vertex AI RAG Engine, AlloyDB AI, BigQuery vector search, Vertex AI Search, Gemini File Search, Firestore vector search, Cloud SQL pgvector, ADK+RAG, Genkit) with exact titles+URLs+key code. Managed RAG Oct 2026 (Gemini File Search, OpenAI file_search, Bedrock KB, Azure AI Search agentic retrieval), framework versions (LangChain/LangGraph 1.x, LlamaIndex, Haystack 2.x, DSPy 3), top GitHub repos + stars.
08-videos-sota-2026

RAG frontier 2025-2026: key papers, trends (agentic search, reasoning + retrieval, context engineering, "RAG is dead?" vs 1M-10M contexts, knowledge graph revival, test-time compute for retrieval). YouTube/courses (LangChain RAG from scratch, DeepLearning.AI, AI Engineer World Fair, Jerry Liu, Jason Liu, Google Cloud Tech): title, channel, URL, takeaways.

decks.title: Customizing modern AI: SFT, RL, RAG and data-centric AI
decks.description: How to adapt foundation models with supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning and RAG, and how to design, generate, curate, label and evaluate the data that makes it work.
decks.brief: "Customizing modern AI - SFT, RL, RAG" + "Data-Centric AI - modern dataset design and synthesis": dataset design and contracts, metrics and coverage, quality and drift, label noise and agreement, active learning, entity/time/group leakage, LLM/RAG datasets, synthetic data with verification, AI eval design, slice metrics, cost-sensitive thresholds, full lifecycle design -> generate -> select -> curate -> label -> denoise -> quality card. State of the art (Oct 2026) with real-world examples and open challenges. SFT (LoRA/QLoRA/DoRA, TRL, Unsloth, Gemma/Vertex tuning), RL (RLHF/PPO, DPO family, GRPO, RLVR, reward models, RFT), RAG (pipeline + agentic RAG + when to choose RAG vs FT). Code snippets about every third slide; codelabs/repos quoted with URLs.
decks.ctx: a university-grade 60-slide deck titled around "Customizing modern AI - SFT, RL, RAG" and "Data-Centric AI - modern dataset design and synthesis", state of the art as of Oct 2026, real-world examples and open challenges. Full lifecycle: design -> generate -> select -> curate -> label -> denoise -> quality card.

topics: 01-customization-map

The customization decision map: prompting/context engineering vs RAG vs SFT vs preference tuning vs RL; cost, data needs, latency, when each wins; real-world examples (companies). Also managed tuning: Vertex AI Gemini supervised tuning + preference tuning, OpenAI fine-tuning + reinforcement fine-tuning (RFT), Anthropic/Bedrock fine-tuning, Together/Fireworks. RAG-in-brief for this deck (pipeline + agentic RAG + when RAG beats FT). Numbers.
02-sft

Supervised fine-tuning SOTA: full FT vs PEFT (LoRA, QLoRA, DoRA, rsLoRA, PiSSA), instruction tuning, chat templates, packing, loss masking, catastrophic forgetting, model merging (TIES, DARE, SLERP), distillation. Tools: Hugging Face TRL SFTTrainer (latest version), PEFT, Unsloth, Axolotl, LLaMA-Factory, torchtune, Keras/KerasHub Gemma LoRA. Google codelabs + Kaggle notebooks on Gemma fine-tuning (exact titles+URLs). Code.
03-rl

RL for LLMs SOTA: RLHF with PPO (InstructGPT), reward models, DPO, IPO, KTO, ORPO, SimPO, GRPO (DeepSeekMath / DeepSeek-R1), DAPO, Dr.GRPO, RLVR (verifiable rewards), RLAIF/Constitutional AI, process vs outcome reward models, reward hacking, agentic/multi-turn RL, rubric rewards. Tools: TRL (DPOTrainer, GRPOTrainer), verl, OpenRLHF, Unsloth GRPO, OpenAI RFT. Code + numbers.
04-dataset-design-contracts

Dataset design: datasheets for datasets, data cards (Google Data Cards Playbook), dataset/data contracts (schema, semantics, SLAs; tools: Great Expectations, Pandera, Soda, dbt contracts), coverage metrics and taxonomy coverage, slice definitions, quality and drift (PSI, KS, JS divergence, embedding drift; Evidently, WhyLabs), real examples.
05-labels-noise-active

Labeling: label noise, inter-annotator agreement (Cohen kappa, Fleiss, Krippendorff alpha), confident learning (cleanlab), dataset cartography, LLM-as-annotator and agreement with humans, active learning (uncertainty, diversity, BADGE, core-set), weak supervision (Snorkel), annotation tools (Label Studio, Argilla). Leakage: entity/group/time leakage, GroupKFold, temporal splits, near-duplicate dedup (MinHash/LSH), benchmark contamination in LLMs. Code (scikit-learn, cleanlab).
06-llm-rag-datasets-synthetic

LLM + RAG datasets and synthetic data with verification: pretraining data curation (FineWeb, FineWeb-Edu, DCLM, Dolma, NeMo Curator, DataTrove), instruction data (Self-Instruct, Evol-Instruct, Magpie, Persona Hub, Tulu 3 data, OpenThoughts), data selection (LESS, DSIR, quality classifiers, dedup), synthetic generation with verification (execution checks, unit tests, LLM judges, reward models, rejection sampling, constitutional filters), model collapse risks, distilabel, synthetic RAG eval sets (RAGAS testset generation). Real numbers.
07-eval-design

AI eval design: eval-driven development, golden sets, slice metrics, confidence intervals/bootstrap, calibration (ECE), cost-sensitive thresholds (cost matrices, expected cost, ROC operating point), LLM-as-judge pitfalls + agreement, pairwise/Elo, eval frameworks (lm-evaluation-harness, Inspect AI, HELM, OpenAI evals, promptfoo, DeepEval, Vertex AI Gen AI evaluation service), quality card / model card, full data lifecycle design -> generate -> select -> curate -> label -> denoise -> quality card.
08-sota-examples-challenges

State of the art + real-world examples 2025-2026 (e.g. Tulu 3, OLMo 2/3, DeepSeek-R1, Qwen3, Gemma 3, Llama data recipes, Phi synthetic-data recipes, company case studies of fine-tuning/RL/RAG) and open challenges (reward hacking, data contamination, synthetic data collapse, eval saturation, privacy, licensing, long-tail coverage). Best Google codelabs, GitHub repos (huggingface/trl, cleanlab, argilla, distilabel, ragas, unsloth) and YouTube talks/courses (title, URL, takeaways).
